strategies.name: v5 + risk throttle
strategies.family: Reversal bot: doji or hammer at a 30-day low
strategies.headline: Buys a confirmed reversal off a 30-session low, only when the market is healthy and the stock is above its 200-day average. About 8 signals a year across the whole universe.
entry: Pattern bar: its low is the lowest low of the last 30 sessions.

The pattern bar is a doji (body no more than 10% of its range) or a strict hammer (body at least 5% of range, lower wick at least 2.5 times the body, upper wick no more than half the body, close in the top quarter).
The next bar closes above the pattern bar's high plus 0.10 times ATR14.
That confirmation bar closes in the top 30% of its own range.
RSI14 is at least 45 on the confirmation bar. RSI and ATR are SMA-smoothed, not Wilder, which differs from TradingView.
The close is above the stock's 200-day SMA.
Confirmation-bar volume is at least 1.3 times its 20-day average.
Entry is the next session's open. The confirmation close is never fillable on an end-of-day scanner.
exit: Stop: the pattern bar's low, with no buffer. Risk (R) is entry minus stop.
At +1R sell half and move the stop to entry.
The remaining half exits at +4R. The normal best case is therefore +2.5R, not +4R.
No trailing stop and no time stop. If one bar touches both stop and target, the stop is assumed.
Costs of 0.20% round trip are charged in R, so very tight stops pay a lot.
filters: Regime gate: new entries only while more than 50% of the whole universe trades above its own 200-day average. Each market uses its own breadth.
At most 5 positions open at once. Extra signals are skipped, not queued.
Risk throttle: size is halved while v5's own total-R curve is below its 50-day mean. The multiplier is frozen at entry.
Trade the whole list. Never rank or filter symbols by their past results under this strategy.
Use it as an overlay: about 0.5% of the account per trade, 0.25% when the throttle is on.
strategies.verdict: Chosen under the strictest protocol: selected on 2000-2015, confirmed on an untouched 2016-2026 half, positive in all 4 market and era cells. Without the throttle the drawdown is -9.55% and growth at a 20% drawdown budget is 4.68%. It is too sparse to carry an account alone, so it works as an overlay that is almost uncorrelated with long equity exposure (+0.06).
caveats: The universe uses today's index members projected backward, so older years read optimistically.
The breadth gate is directionally right but not calibrated.
Weekly-timeframe signals are scanned but were never backtested and are labelled unvalidated.
rejected: Resistance-becomes-support filter: no stable edge (t about 0.65) and the sign flips at looser settings.
Tighter position caps, breadth thresholds and stop-width limits: they cut drawdown only by trading less.
Releasing the break-even stop: better on the full sample but splits 7.20% and 2.56% across halves, so it is fitted.
Ranking symbols by past performance: split-half correlation of 0.18 is noise.
Win rate as an objective: across 1,344 configs it correlates negatively with total profit (r = -0.21).

strategies.name: v6 shadow build
strategies.family: Reversal bot: shorter lookback
strategies.headline: v5 with an 11-session swing low, an RSI floor of 30 and an EMA200 trend filter. Tracked live next to v5 so the two can be compared on real signals.
entry: Pattern bar: its low is the lowest low of the last 11 sessions (v5 uses 30).
Same doji or strict hammer shape rules as v5.
Confirmation bar closes above the pattern high plus 0.10 times ATR14 and in the top 30% of its range.
RSI14 at least 30 (v5 uses 45).
Close above the 200-day EMA (v5 uses the 200-day SMA).
Volume at least 1.3 times the 20-day average. Entry at the next session's open.
exit: Same as v5: stop at the pattern low, half off at +1R with the stop to entry, the rest at +4R.
No trailing or time stop. Costs 0.20% round trip.
filters: Same breadth gate and 5-position cap as v5.
No risk throttle: it was measured on v6 and lowered return at equal drawdown.
strategies.verdict: 2.6 times the trade frequency of v5 with growth at a 20% drawdown budget of 7.67% against v5's 4.68%, and the hold-out average R (0.354) above the training half (0.258). It has not yet been through v5's full select-early, confirm-late protocol, so v5 stays the live pick.
caveats: Its raw drawdown at 1% risk is larger than v5's because it holds more trades at once, so size it smaller.
rejected: Waiting 20-30 bars after the swing low before confirming (Reading A): no edge out of sample (hold-out average R -0.0008, t = 1.77).
RSI at least 30 alone, or an any-of-EMA20/50/200 trend filter alone, on the 30-bar window: both lowered growth at a common drawdown.
The any-EMA trend filter is the weakest element tested, because the close is above the 20-day EMA most of the time.

strategies.name: Logic 3: double bottom and engulfing
strategies.family: Double bottom, bullish engulfing, EMA cross, breakout
strategies.status_label: Validated, not live
strategies.headline: A second low near the first, a bullish engulfing candle, then a breakout above the latest bullish candle. The only build that has passed the full honest protocol, but not yet put into live scanning. Scored with 2008 and 2020 excluded, the owner's standing convention for this backtest.
entry: A big downtrend into the first bottom: the 40-bar high minus the low is at least 3 ATR and at least 5%, with EMA5 below EMA20 and the close below EMA50.
A second bottom 1 to 9 candles later within 0.5 ATR of the first, with a bounce of at least 0.5 ATR between them. Adjacent lows (tweezer bottoms) are accepted.
A bullish engulfing candle, or a dragonfly doji, within 5 bars of the second bottom.
EMA5 crosses above EMA20 at or within 5 bars after that candle.
The double bottom retraces 38.2% to 61.8% of the prior 90-bar up-leg.
A buy-stop rests above the high of the most recent bullish candle for up to 5 bars, and breakout volume must be at least 1.2 times its 20-day average.
exit: Stop: 0.5 ATR below the lower of the two bottoms. Skip the trade if risk is over 15% of price.
Target: 2.0R. No break-even move, trail, scale-out or time stop.
If one bar touches both stop and target, the stop is assumed.
Costs of 0.20% round trip.
filters: One position per symbol and at most 8 open at once.
Size it through the same risk throttle as v5 and v6; its monthly correlation to v6 is only +0.14.
strategies.verdict: 768 configurations were tested with the grid fixed in advance. Selected on 2000-2015 only and run once on 2016-2026 it returned +0.4253R (a 23% haircut from the +0.5487R selection value, still t = 4.66). A walk-forward from 2010, re-selecting each year, returned +0.4202R over 409 trades using only 5 distinct configs in 19 years. Losing years: 2 of 27. With 2008 and 2020 excluded from scoring (the owner's standing convention for this backtest), the edge gets stronger, not weaker (avg R 0.4929 to 0.5223) -- the other four configs tested the same way (spec, TUNED, TUNED2, TUNED3) mostly got WORSE once those two crash years were dropped, which is the honest signal that this build's edge isn't a crash-reversal artifact the way theirs partly are. This re-scored the chosen config; it did not re-run the TRAIN-only selection itself with those years excluded, which is the next thing to do before sizing real risk on the difference.
caveats: Entry timing is worth about half the edge. Entering at the next open instead of on the intraday buy-stop roughly halves growth, so this needs a resting stop order. Check the fill assumption on real intraday data first.
The universe is survivorship-biased.
At about 23 trades a year the live sample takes months to say anything, so paper trade it alongside v5 and v6.
2008 and 2020 are excluded from every metric above by dropping the trades that exit in those years, not by deleting price bars -- see the 2008/2020 write-up for the full before/after comparison.
rejected: Any break-even move: the single worst change on the board (+0.75R costs -0.107R).
3.0R target: strong on training (0.472) and gone on test (0.240).
Breadth gate on this setup: 0.251 on training, 0.125 on test.
Lows within 0.30 ATR, a cross within 3 bars, or engulfing strictly after the second bottom: all fitted to training.
Dragonfly doji as a required bottom shape: only 19 trades.
Fibonacci zone as a sizing tilt or a ranking rule: no gain in compounding.
ATR trailing stops and an 8-bar breakout window.

strategies.name: S1: double bottom and engulfing (frozen build)
strategies.family: Three-strategy study S1/S2/S3
strategies.headline: Big downtrend, then a double bottom 10-20 candles apart, a bullish engulfing candle, an EMA5 cross above EMA20, and a break of the recent candle's high. Scanned live and paper-traded.
entry: Big downtrend into the first bottom, then a double bottom 10 to 20 candles apart with lows within 0.5 ATR.
A bullish engulfing candle with volume at least 1.2 times the prior bar's.
EMA5 closes above EMA20.
A buy-stop above the recent candle's high; the actual fill price is what gets recorded.
exit: Stop below the double bottom with a 0.10 ATR buffer; skip if risk is over 15%.
Target: 2.5R. No break-even, trail or scale-out.
Costs 0.20% round trip.
filters: Not capped or throttled in the paper-trade book. The study pooled it at 12 positions, so live per-trade R is comparable but portfolio return reads slightly high.
strategies.verdict: The table shows the 'S1 tuned' research row, ranked first on the training years. In the 2010-2026 walk-forward the live frozen build was expected to win about 45.4% of trades at +0.56R. The hold-out half is weaker than training (0.62R against 0.77R) but clearly positive.
caveats: Fills happen intraday on a buy-stop, so the same execution risk as Logic 3 applies.
rejected: The checklist as first written (S1 spec): +0.2267R, about a third of the tuned result.
Entering at the next open instead of on the stop: +0.57R against +0.71R.

strategies.name: S2: trend, Fibonacci pullback, dragonfly doji
strategies.family: Three-strategy study S1/S2/S3
strategies.status_label: Not carried forward
strategies.headline: An uptrend, a retracement into the 50-61.8% Fibonacci band, then a dragonfly doji. Buys the next open. The weakest of the three and left out of the live blend.
entry: An uptrend in the first half of the window.
A retracement into the 50% to 61.8% Fibonacci band.
A dragonfly doji, then buy at the next open.
exit: Structural stop and an R-multiple target, with the same 0.20% costs as the other studies.
filters: Shared portfolio cap and cost model with S1 and S3.
strategies.verdict: The 'robust' version is the only S2 with a positive hold-out, and that edge is nearly gone (test average R 0.0886, t = 1.04). The tuned version scored 0.0588 on the test years.
caveats: Not part of the recommended blend.
rejected: The checklist as written: +0.2622R but only 173 trades and t = 2.31.

strategies.name: S3: range break (frozen build)
strategies.family: Three-strategy study S1/S2/S3
strategies.headline: Price ranges at one level for 10-15 candles, then closes outside the zone. Buys the next open on an upside break. Long only, 2R target.
entry: Price holds the same level for 10 to 15 candles, forming a tight zone.
A close outside the upper edge of the zone.
Buy the next session's open.
exit: Target: 2.0R from a structural stop.
No break-even, trail or scale-out. Costs 0.20% round trip.
filters: Long only. The both-directions version at 1:1 scored +0.0357R and was dropped.
strategies.verdict: Holds up on the hold-out half (test 0.2594, t = 2.87) and in both markets. A higher-frequency variant ('S3 freq', 849 trades) scored 11.1% growth at a 20% drawdown budget on the test years.
caveats: Edge is smaller in the US (+0.33R) than in India (+0.23R on fewer trades).
rejected: Both directions at 1:1: no edge (t = 1.41).

strategies.name: S1 + S3 blend (cap 12)
strategies.family: Three-strategy study S1/S2/S3
strategies.status_label: Recommended blend
strategies.headline: Run S1 tuned and S3 frequent together with up to 12 positions open. The headline figure is in-sample; the clean out-of-sample figure from 2010 is lower and is the one to plan around.
entry: Signals come from the S1 and S3 detectors described above.
Both run on the same price cache and the same cost model.
exit: Each leg keeps its own exits: S1 at 2.5R, S3 at 2.0R.
filters: Up to 12 positions open across both strategies (14 at the peak in the walk-forward).
The three strategies' returns correlate only about 0.19 with each other.
strategies.verdict: The numbers shown are the frozen 2010-2026 out-of-sample run: 923 trades, +0.3358R, 12.36% growth at a 20% drawdown budget, drawdown -26.9% at 1% risk. The in-sample 'recommended' blend scored 16.86% (+0.4131R, t = 9.1, hold-out 0.3887), and the annually re-fitted walk-forward scored 11.41%. Plan around the lower, honest numbers.
caveats: The worst recent stretch: 2025 was -9.4% and 2026 is -5.6% to date in the walk-forward.
Drawdown at 1% risk is large; size down to about 0.7-0.9% per trade for a 20% drawdown.
rejected: Annual re-selection of settings (11.41%) did worse than freezing the 2010 settings (13.13%), so constant re-tuning is not helping.

strategies.name: Accumulation Bot v2.3
strategies.family: Smart-money swing breakout, US and India
strategies.headline: Finds stocks that institutions appear to be accumulating, then waits for a tight-base breakout on heavy volume in a confirmed market uptrend. Quality first: few trades, high win rate.
entry: A. Preliminary: price over $5, daily dollar volume over $20M, tight spread, earnings date known, and SPY or QQQ in an uptrend.

B. Seven points: price trend, moving-average alignment, relative strength (RS line near its 6-month high and the industry group in the top 30%), up/down volume and accumulation days (shown as support only in version 2), a tight base no deeper than 12%, and sound fundamentals.
C. Plan: entry within 3% of the pivot, risk no more than 8% of price, reward to risk at least 2:1, no earnings surprise inside the window.
Breakout volume at least 1.75 times the 20-day average. Grade A+ needs 2 times or more.
Only buys when the market regime reads Confirmed uptrend (the buy gate).
exit: Stop below the base; move to break-even at +1.5R; trail the 21-day EMA; time stop at 60 days.
Size: 1% account risk per trade (A+ takes 100% of that, A takes 75%), at most 8 positions and 20% in one name.
filters: India uses the same rules on the Nifty 500 with rupee thresholds (price over Rs 50, turnover over Rs 20 crore).
Days with no new trading bar are skipped automatically.
strategies.verdict: Version 2 raised the win rate from 55% to 64% and profit per trade from +0.28R to +0.60R against version 1, on 200 large caps from 2001 to 2026. A+ only: 40 trades, 68% win, +0.74R, profit factor 3.33.
caveats: That test used a hand-picked list of today's winners with rules chosen on the same data, so confirm on the full universe and paper trade before sizing up.
The India rules were tuned on US data. Run the backtest on IN first.
Fundamentals, earnings dates, spreads and institutional data have no free point-in-time history, so they only apply to the live scan, not the backtest.
rejected: Version 1's looser rules (50th-percentile industry, up/down volume and accumulation days required, 1.5 times volume).

strategies.name: Revenue trend and price dip
strategies.family: Screen: growing revenue, oversold price
strategies.status_label: Watch list only
strategies.headline: Looks for companies with a rising revenue record whose share price has dipped 15-40% from its 52-week high and just turned up. Use it as a watch list, not for sizing trades.
entry: Close is 15% to 40% below its 52-week high.
RSI14 was at or below 40 within the last 3 sessions, and today is a reversal day (close up and RSI up).
The market gate: the equal-weight index of that market must be above its 200-day average, otherwise signals are blocked.

Revenue over the last 5 fiscal years is positive: CAGR above zero and at least 3 of 4 yearly changes up. US uses SEC EDGAR when a contact is set in revenue_dip_config.json, otherwise Yahoo; India uses Yahoo.
exit: Stop: 2.5 times ATR14, clipped to 5-12% below the close.
Trail the stop to the highest close minus 3 ATR.
Exit after 80 trading days.
Risk 0.75% of equity per trade, position at most 12% of equity.
filters: Revenue is fetched only for stocks with a dip signal or in the dip zone, then cached for 14 days.
strategies.verdict: Tested on 200 US stocks from 2001 to 2026 (today's survivors). With the market filter and ATR exits it earned about 11% a year with a -23% worst drawdown, but did not beat simply holding those stocks. With a stock list chosen only from past data it earned about 5% a year. The revenue filter itself has not been tested yet.
caveats: Screening output only. Do not size real trades from it yet.

strategies.name: Market context classifier
strategies.family: Structural pre-filter: what is this stock's chart doing right now
strategies.status_label: Classifier, not a signal
strategies.headline: Tags every stock with one of six structural states -- new ATH breakout, inside a 300-day sideways range, below or above its daily trendline, or pulling back shallow vs. deep inside an uptrend -- before any entry logic is applied to it. Not a buy/sell signal on its own.
entry: New ATH: today's close exceeds the full-history close high, and that prior high had stood for at least 60 bars (a base, not a level set last week).
300-day range: no new ATH, and net price progress over the last 300 sessions is under half the range's own width (sideways, not trending).

Trendline direction: fit a line through the last 3 confirmed swing highs (descending) or swing lows (ascending), a standard causal fractal -- a swing point only confirms 5 bars after it happens, so there is no lookahead.
Descending trendline: BELOW it is DOWNTREND_INTACT, a close back ABOVE it is DOWNTREND_BREAK.
Ascending trendline: retracement = (most recent swing high minus today's close) / (that high minus the swing low before it). <=50% is UPTREND_PULLBACK_SMALL, >50% is UPTREND_PULLBACK_DEEP.
No match (too few confirmed swing points, or neither trendline direction qualifies) is UNCLASSIFIED.
exit: Not applicable -- this assigns a context tag, it does not open or close positions.
filters: Evaluated top to bottom, first match wins: NEW_ATH_BREAKOUT, then RANGE_CORRECTION_300D, then the trendline read.

Runs daily in scan_US.bat / scan_India.bat and writes LATEST_CONTEXT_<market>.json to the scans folder; only the actionable tags (new ATH, downtrend break, small/deep pullback) ship rows to this page -- the sideways and unclassified buckets, usually 70-80% of the universe, show as counts only.
strategies.verdict: Reconstructed from a whiteboard sketch on 2026-10-30 and implemented directly -- no backtest behind the tag boundaries yet (the 50% RANGE_PROGRESS_RATIO and the 50% retracement split are textbook defaults, not fitted to this project's own data the way v5/v6 were). Use it to decide which existing bot's signals are worth acting on today, not as a standalone edge.
caveats: RANGE_CORRECTION_300D caught 78% of the US+India universe on the first live run -- the sideways-progress threshold likely needs tightening once checked against known cases.

A retracement over 100% (seen live on a handful of names) means price broke below the swing low that started the up-leg -- the ascending trendline is stale, treat UPTREND_PULLBACK_DEEP with a >100% figure as a broken trend, not a deep dip.
Classifies structure only; carries no opinion on entry price, stop or size.

strategies.name: Analog setup scanner (stage 1 + stages 2-4)
strategies.family: Context gate, then weekly breakout validated by the stock's own history, 4H trade plan
strategies.status_label: First pass, not yet tuned
strategies.headline: Combines the context classifier above with stages 2-4: for each stock currently tagged a fresh breakout, finds every prior weekly base-and-breakout in its own history, backtests how the retest actually played out each time, and only produces today's entry/stop/target plan if at least 2 of those precedents confirmed. This card is stage 1 AND stages 2-4 run together, not stage 2-4 alone.
entry: Stage 1 (context gate): the stock's CURRENT market_context.py tag must be NEW_ATH_BREAKOUT or DOWNTREND_BREAK -- the two tags that mean the chart just broke a level today. Everything else (sideways, intact up/downtrend, deep pullback) is excluded before stages 2-4 even run.

Stage 2 (weekly): a base is 5 consecutive weekly bars whose high-low range stays within 12% of the base's own low; a breakout is the next weekly bar closing above the base's high. Scanned across the stock's full weekly history, each event skips the scan past it so zones never overlap.

Stage 3 (daily, per historical event): search up to 20 daily bars for the 1st bar whose low comes back within 1% of the broken level, then the first bar after that which closes back above it (confirmation). Entry = next bar's open. Stop = the retest low, discarded as noise if under 0.5% of price. The trade is then walked forward up to 60 bars to see whether it actually hit +2R or the stop first.

Stage 4 (live): only produced when the stock's MOST RECENT weekly event is currently inside its own retest window (touched the level, not yet confirmed, not yet failed, not timed out) AND at least 2 of its prior events confirmed AND the stage-1 context gate passes. Target is sized off the median R actually achieved by those confirmed analogs, not assumed.
exit: Stop: the live retest's low.
Break-even: +1R, the same convention v5/v6 use.
Target: entry + (median achieved R of the confirmed historical analogs) x risk.
filters: Stage-1 context gate (NEW_ATH_BREAKOUT or DOWNTREND_BREAK) is a hard requirement, enforced in code -- analog_setup.py calls the same classify_context() function market_context.py uses, not just a run-order assumption.

Hard gate: fewer than 2 CONFIRMED historical analogs (not just 2 prior base+breakout events) and the setup is not surfaced at all -- a base that occurred before but never completed its own retest isn't evidence this works for this stock.
Runs daily in scan_US.bat / scan_India.bat, after the context classifier. Writes LATEST_ANALOG_<market>.json.
strategies.verdict: Transcribed from a hand-marked-up chart (MINDA CORP LTD) on 2026-10-30 and implemented directly -- no walk-forward or out-of-sample protocol behind it yet, the way v5/v6/logic3 went through. The first version ran stages 2-4 without actually checking the stage-1 context tag and surfaced 22 US + 22 India stocks; adding the real stage-1 gate (2026-10-30) cut that to 1 US (CFG) + 1 India (JSWSTEEL) on the same data -- stage 1 is doing real filtering, not a rubber stamp.
caveats: The whiteboard asked for a 4H chart at stages 3-4; this project has no intraday data pipeline and free sources only cover 60-730 days, far short of what multi-year-old analogs need. Stages 3-4 run on DAILY bars instead -- a fully-automatable proxy, but it loses the finer structure a 4H chart would show inside each daily bar.
Z_MIN (5 weeks), the 12% base-width cap, the 1% retest tolerance and the 2R backtest target are first-pass defaults, not tuned the way v5/v6's constants were.
Per-symbol only: a stock with a short or quiet history may never clear the 2-confirmed-analog gate, regardless of how good today's setup looks.
No position sizing, portfolio cap or regime gate -- unlike v5/v6/logic3, nothing here limits how many of these 44 names could be taken at once.

strategies.name: Base + breakout scanner (stage 1 + stage 2)
strategies.family: Context gate, then weekly base-and-breakout detection only -- no backtest
strategies.status_label: Wider candidate list, not a signal
strategies.headline: The wider screen between the context classifier and the analog scanner: every stock currently tagged a fresh breakout (stage 1) that also has a weekly base-and-breakout within the last 8 weeks (stage 2) -- no retest backtest, no entry/stop/target math, no 2-confirmed-analog gate. Shows what's forming before precedent-validation narrows it down to a trade plan.
entry: Stage 1 (context gate): the stock's CURRENT market_context.py tag must be NEW_ATH_BREAKOUT or DOWNTREND_BREAK, same as the analog scanner's gate.

Stage 2 (weekly): a base is 5 consecutive weekly bars whose high-low range stays within 12% of the base's own low; a breakout is the next weekly bar closing above the base's high. Scanned across the stock's full weekly history, each event skips the scan past it so zones never overlap.
Recency filter: only the stock's MOST RECENT weekly base+breakout counts, and only if it happened within the last 8 weekly bars -- otherwise it's old history, not a current candidate.
exit: Not applicable -- this is a detection screen, not a trade plan. See the analog scanner above for actual entry/stop/target levels once a setup has enough validated history.
filters: Both the stage-1 context gate and the stage-2 base+breakout detection are shared code with the context classifier and the analog scanner (classify_context(), find_base_breakout_events()).
No MIN_ANALOGS gate here -- that's what makes this list wider than the analog scanner's. Cross-reference against the analog scanner card to see which of these already have validated precedent.
Runs daily in scan_US.bat / scan_India.bat, after the analog scanner. Writes LATEST_BASEBREAKOUT_<market>.json.
strategies.verdict: Added 2026-10-30 as a third card between the context classifier (very wide, no stage-2 structure) and the analog scanner (narrow, fully validated). First live run: 23 US + 3 India candidates, against the analog scanner's 1 + 1 on the same data -- confirms this sits where intended, between the two.
caveats: The 8-week recency window is a first-pass default, not tuned.
No historical win-rate or R:R behind these -- that's deliberately what the analog scanner adds on top of this list.
Per-symbol only, like the analog scanner: no position sizing, portfolio cap or regime gate.

strategies.name: Weinstein Stage-2 scanner (30-week MA bull market bottom)
strategies.family: Weekly: Stage 1 base then Stage 2 breakout, read off the 30-week MA
strategies.status_label: Backtested, scanned live
strategies.headline: Stan Weinstein's stage analysis on a single 30-week MA: the average has to have been falling, then flatten into a base, before a weekly close back above it (with the MA itself turning up and volume confirming) counts as a Stage-2 breakout. Transcribed from five reference weekly charts with arrows marking the MA's turn, then backtested on this project's own 1,003-name universe.
entry: Stage 1 base: the 30-week MA was net lower than it was a year (52 weeks) before the base started, then flattened -- at most 3% drift over the 10 weeks right before the breakout.
Stage 2 cross: a weekly close above the 30-week MA, with the prior week's close at or below it -- a fresh cross, not price already extended above.
The MA itself has stopped falling: this week's MA value is at or above last week's.
Breakout-week volume is at least 1.5 times its 10-week average -- Weinstein's own confirmation rule.
Entry is the following week's open.
exit: Stop: the lowest low of the 26 weeks before the breakout (the base low), no buffer.
Exit: the first weekly CLOSE back below the 30-week MA -- the stage reversal itself. No fixed target, no trailing stop, no time stop.
Costs of 0.20% round trip are charged in R, same as the rest of the reversal bot.
filters: Indicators are computed on the full continuous weekly series; only the base-flatness and prior-downtrend checks look back from the week before the cross, so there is no look-ahead.
Runs daily (weekly-bar) in scan_US.bat / scan_India.bat, after the base+breakout scanner. Writes LATEST_WEINSTEIN_<market>.json.
No market breadth gate, relative-strength filter or position cap yet -- see caveats.
strategies.verdict: Built 2026-10-30 from two reference images of weekly charts (five examples) with arrows pointing at the 30-week MA's turn. A 7-variant sweep confirmed the Stage-1 structure is most of the edge: stripping it to a naive 'close crosses a rising 30-week MA' (no prior-downtrend or flattening check, no volume) gave 39x more trades at a third the average R and 12x worse drawdown relative to total return. A tighter stop at the MA instead of the base low looked better on avg R but was 9x worse on drawdown -- same 'tight stop is not free leverage' lesson as v5. Asked to exclude 2008 and 2020 as crash years: 2008 was a genuine drag (14 trades, -5.7R) but 2020 was the single best entry-year in the dataset (48 trades, +102R, ~18% of all-time return -- the COVID V-recovery is the cleanest version of this pattern in the sample), so the live rule excludes neither.
caveats: Weekly stops are wide (median ~18-20% of price) -- size positions for that explicitly, don't risk-size the way a tight daily stop would let you.
No market breadth gate yet, unlike v5/ema20confirm -- a likely next addition (see docs).
No relative-strength-vs-index filter yet, even though it's Weinstein's other core screening criterion alongside the stage.
No position sizing or portfolio cap: with 26 signals/year clustering at real market bottoms, uncapped exposure can stack correlated longs in the same quarter.
No live track record yet, like basebreakout and ema20confirm.
rejected: Stop at the MA value instead of the base low: avg R looked better (2.16 vs 0.88) but max drawdown was 9x worse (-148R vs -16R) -- a tight stop inflates R-multiples on both sides.
Fixed 4R target instead of the MA-cross stage exit: cut total return nearly in half (556R to 291R) -- the edge lives in a small number of trades that run for over a year.
Excluding 2008 AND 2020 entries as 'crash years': nets negative vs. the unfiltered rule, because 2020's entries were the best cohort in the dataset, not a risk to avoid.

strategies.name: EMA20 cross + confirm 1.8R
strategies.family: Reversal bot: EMA20 cross, next-candle confirmation, liquidity-filtered India
strategies.status_label: Scanned live, no live track record yet
strategies.universe: 1,003 names: S&P 500 + Nifty 500, India narrowed to the top 250 by $-volume at scan time
strategies.headline: Buys the next session's open when a stock's close crosses above its 20 EMA and the next candle confirms above that close, with the market healthy and the stock above its own 200-day average. Started as a chart screenshot on 2026-10-29, then tuned and validated against this project's own universe.
entry: Signal bar: close crosses above the 20 EMA (the prior close was at or below it).
Confirmation bar: the next candle closes above the signal bar's close.
Close is above the stock's own 200-day SMA.
The market's breadth gate is open: more than 50% of the whole universe trades above its own 200-day average (same gate as v5/v6, each market scored separately).
India only: the symbol is in the top 250 India names by trailing $ volume (close times volume, averaged over the last 500 bars) -- a liquidity proxy; this project has no market-cap feed.
Entry is the next session's open.
exit: Stop: entry minus (1.25 times ATR14, plus 5 points). Risk (R) is entry minus stop.
Target: entry plus 1.8 times risk. No break-even move, trail, scale-out or time stop.
If one bar touches both stop and target, the stop is assumed.
Costs of 0.20% round trip are charged in R, same as the rest of the reversal bot.
filters: Same breadth gate and 5-position cap as v5/v6.
India universe narrowed to the top 250 by $ volume, recomputed from trailing data at every scan, not a fixed list.
No risk throttle, unlike v5: not yet measured with one.
strategies.verdict: Transcribed from a chart screenshot (VOLTAS LTD, 1D) on 2026-10-29 as a plain EMA20-cross-and-confirm rule with a 1:1.4 target. Unfiltered it backtested flat-to-negative (avg R -0.006 to -0.022 depending on the data snapshot, clearly negative out of sample). The decay traced almost entirely to India post-2015 (avg R -0.107) while the US side stayed stable (+0.016). v5's own trend200 + breadth>50% filters rescued it to modestly positive (avg R +0.036, t=1.06). Seven more filter ideas were then tested against the data and rejected -- see below. Narrowing India to its most liquid 250 names, widening the stop and a neighbourhood sweep of the R:R target did help: the final build (1.25xATR stop, 1.8R target, liquid-250 India) scores avg R +0.2584, t=5.04, PF 1.46, 743 trades 2000-2026, 4 of 4 market-and-era cells positive, with train (+0.265) and test (+0.255) nearly identical -- no sign of the earlier decay. Every neighbour of R:R, ATR multiplier, liquidity cut, trend length and breadth threshold in the sensitivity sweep stayed positive, which is the main reason to trust this more than the first filtered attempt.
caveats: No live track record: this has not been through the months of paper-trading v5/v6/S1/S3 went through before being trusted. Watch it before sizing.
The liquidity cut is $ volume (close times volume), not true market capitalization -- this project has no free market-cap feed.
Rolling 3-year windows were checked separately; most are positive, but the newest ones were the softest part of the sample, so treat the most recent months as the part most likely to disappoint.
Costs, the breadth gate and the position cap are shared with v5/v6 by convention, not re-derived for this rule specifically.

2026-10-30 multi-timeframe study (see the two cards below and the MTF spec doc): waiting for an hourly intraday breakout before taking this daily entry was tested and made results WORSE (avg R +0.412 on the subset that eventually confirmed intraday, if bought blind at the open, vs +0.136 if you wait for that confirmation and chase the higher price). Keep entering at the next day's open exactly as written above.
rejected: A percentage-based stop buffer (0.5% of price instead of a flat +5 points): actively harmful, t=-2.38 -- for most of this universe that buffer was far tighter than 5 points, and tight stops lost.
Confirmation-bar volume at least 1.2 times its 20-day average: average R went negative (t=-0.27).
RSI14 at least 45 on the confirmation bar: average R dropped to roughly zero (t=-0.06).
Requiring the confirmation bar to also make a higher high: no real improvement (t=0.21).
Requiring the confirmation close to clear the signal close by at least 0.15 ATR: improved the full-sample average, but only on the training years -- the post-2015 period got worse, not better.

Gating this daily entry on weekly-timeframe trend alignment (weekly close > weekly EMA20): only filtered ~5% of trades and made the survivors slightly worse (t 5.01->4.42, PF 1.49->1.43) -- the existing 200-day trend filter already captures most of this.

Waiting for an hourly intraday breakout above the entry day's opening range before buying: avg R dropped from +0.412 (blind open entry on the same eventually-confirming subset) to +0.136 -- chasing the confirmed price gives back more than the confirmation is worth.

strategies.name: EMA20 cross + confirm, weekly
strategies.family: Reversal bot: same rule as EMA20 cross + confirm 1.8R, run on weekly bars
strategies.status_label: Validated 2026-10-30, not yet scanned live
strategies.universe: 1,003 names: S&P 500 + Nifty 500, resampled to weekly (week ending Friday)
strategies.headline: The same EMA20-cross-and-confirm rule as the daily build, run on weekly candles instead: a weekly close crosses above the weekly 20 EMA, the next week confirms above that close, the weekly trend and market breadth must be healthy. A real but weaker secondary edge -- daily stays the primary system.
entry: Signal bar: weekly close crosses above the weekly 20 EMA (about 100 trading days).
Confirmation bar: the next week's close is above the signal week's close.
Close is above a 40-week SMA (about 200 trading days -- the same /5 scaling this project already uses for weekly breadth, see logic2_scanner.build_regime).
The market's weekly breadth gate is open: more than 50% of the universe above its own 40-week average, computed on weekly bars.
Entry is the next week's open. No India liquidity cut (not yet tested on weekly).
exit: Stop: entry minus (1.25 times weekly ATR14, plus 5 points) -- same constants as the daily build.
Target: entry plus 1.8 times risk. Costs 0.20% round trip, same model as every other build here.
filters: Same breadth-gate convention as v5/v6/daily EMA20confirm, computed on weekly bars.
5-position concurrency cap, same as the rest of the reversal bot.
strategies.verdict: This rule had never been backtested on weekly bars before 2026-10-30 (run_daily_scan.py's own weekly section for v1/v5 has carried a 'not validated' warning for months). It is now validated: 356 trades 2000-2026, t=3.02, PF 1.39, 4 of 4 market-and-era cells positive. It is real but clearly weaker than daily -- the TEST-era t-stat is only 1.54 (barely above noise) and 2025 alone lost -14.84R in the by-year table. Tested as a filter ON TOP of the daily rule (requiring weekly trend alignment for daily entries) and that combination was REJECTED (see the daily card's rejected list) -- weekly works as its own separate, smaller system, not as a daily filter.
caveats: No live scanner yet -- this is a backtest validation only, not wired into run_daily_scan.py's daily output. Treat it the way the project treats a new idea before it earns a scanner: prove it further before building the live plumbing.
Much thinner evidence than daily: about 13-14 trades a year across the whole 1,003-name universe, so a live track record will take a long time to say anything.
2024-2026 was weak on both this and the daily build in the same window -- treat it as one shared regime signal, not two separate problems (see the MTF spec doc).
rejected: See the daily card's rejected list -- the weekly rule has not had its own separate filter-idea sweep yet, only the cross-timeframe test described there.

strategies.name: EMA20 cross + confirm, hourly (pilot)
strategies.family: Reversal bot: same rule as EMA20 cross + confirm 1.8R, literally transplanted to hourly bars
strategies.status_label: Pilot tested 2026-10-30: no edge found
strategies.universe: ~77 liquid names (top ~40 US + ~40 India by trailing $-volume), ~2.2 years of hourly bars (yfinance's live serving window, not this project's 2000-2026 archive)
strategies.headline: The same EMA20-cross-and-confirm rule, unchanged, run on hourly candles. Does not work as a literal timeframe transplant: the flat +5-point stop buffer and the 0.20% round-trip cost, both tuned for daily price ranges, dominate the much smaller hourly ATR. Kept here as a documented negative result, not a live or shadow build.
entry: Identical rule to the daily build (EMA20 cross + next-bar confirm + trend filter), just evaluated on hourly bars instead of daily.
Trend filter scaled by trading hours/day (about 6.5 US, 6.25 India) to approximate the daily rule's 200-session filter.
No breadth gate: the ~77-symbol pilot pool is too small to build a meaningful market-wide breadth signal.
exit: Stop: entry minus (1.25 times hourly ATR14, plus 5 points) -- same constants as daily, NOT rescaled for hourly noise.
Target: entry plus 1.8 times risk. Same 0.20% round-trip cost model as daily.
filters: None beyond the trend filter -- this is the literal transplant, deliberately not yet redesigned for the timeframe.
strategies.verdict: 755 trades over a ~2.2-year pilot come back net negative: avg R -0.026, PF 0.96, only 1 of 4 market-x-half-sample cells positive. A sweep of the stop width (ATR_MULT 1.25 to 4.0) found a tempting peak at 3.0x (t=3.0, PF 1.44), but its neighbours (2.5x: t=0.39, 3.5x: t=1.37, 4.0x: t=-0.15) are all much weaker -- a fitted cliff on a 285-trade sample, not a plateau, by this project's own neighbourhood-sweep standard (see the daily card's verdict). Separately, using hourly bars only to time the ENTRY of an already-confirmed daily signal (wait for an intraday breakout, then buy) was also tested and made the daily rule worse, not better (see the daily card's caveats). Do not trade hourly with this rule in either form yet.
caveats: Short sample: ~2.9 years is the most yfinance serves for 1h bars, nowhere near the daily/weekly rule's 26-year, 2000-2026 evidence.
Small pool: ~77 names vs the full 1,003-name universe, and no breadth gate.

If a standalone hourly system is wanted later: needs a cost model fit for hourly turnover, an ATR-only stop (drop the flat +5 points), and several years more data before any parameter is trusted -- not a rescaled copy of the daily rule.
rejected: ATR_MULT swept from 1.25 to 4.0 at RR=1.8: only 3.0 looked good, and it is a cliff, not a plateau (see verdict) -- not adopted.
Hourly-breakout entry timing on top of the daily signal: avg R dropped from +0.412 (blind open entry) to +0.136 (waiting for the breakout) on the matched subset -- not adopted.

strategies.name: BB Ladder: trough + ascending ladder + breakout
strategies.family: Bollinger Band bottom-fish: lower-band touch, failed-rally ladder, basis-reclaim breakout
strategies.status_label: Validated, not live
strategies.headline: Buys a breakout above a ladder of rising, rejected rally highs that formed after price touched the lower Bollinger Band. Transcribed from a hand-annotated chart on 2026-10-31; the one lever the honest protocol kept is requiring the breakout bar's close, not just its high, back above the Bollinger basis.
entry: Trough: the lowest low of the last 10 bars touches or pierces the lower Bollinger Band (basis = SMA20, band = 2.0x population stdev, TradingView convention), with the basis still falling into the trough so this is a real slide, not noise.

Ladder: searching up to 60 bars forward, at least 2 pivot highs each strictly higher than the last and each still a failed rally (no more than 0.25 ATR above the basis). A pivot that breaks the ladder rule is skipped, not a reset; a low back below the trough kills the setup.

Breakout: within 5 bars of the ladder being confirmed, the first bar whose high clears the highest ladder pivot AND whose close is back above the Bollinger basis -- the one lever the honest protocol kept.
Entry: the trigger price or that bar's open, whichever is higher, so a gap cannot fill cheaper than the actual break.
exit: Stop: just under the trough low, with a 0.10 ATR buffer. Risk (R) is entry minus stop; skipped if risk is over 20% of price.
Target: 2.0R, flat. No break-even move, trail, scale-out or time stop -- deliberately, the same prior v5/Logic 3's own lever sweeps carry forward.
If one bar touches both stop and target, the stop is assumed. Costs of 0.20% round trip.
filters: One detector, two timeframe presets sharing the same price cache: daily (default) and weekly (W-FRI resample of the same daily bars, same costs).
Portfolio cap: 8 concurrent positions, oldest-first.
Hourly is specified, not implemented -- this project has no intraday price source, and Yahoo caps 60-minute history at about 730 days, too short for a real backtest.
strategies.verdict: 192 pre-declared configs, each backtested once: selected on 2000-2015 only and run once on 2016-2026, this lever returned +0.3121R over 189 trades never seen during selection (t=3.43) -- a real pass, though a steeper haircut from its +0.6038R training value than Logic 3 took. The stronger finding: the plain, fixed reclaim-basis build with every other knob left at the chart's own defaults beats BOTH that train-selected pick and a yearly walk-forward re-selection (+0.5456R / t=5.60 fixed, against +0.3121R selected and +0.4025R walk-forward, over the identical 2008-2026 window). Three independent reads of the data -- the one-at-a-time sweep, the train-only pick, and the fixed build beating its own re-optimised descendants -- agree on the same single lever. Confirmed within noise on a second cache rebuilt straight from the current EOD workbooks, 2.5 months of fresh data later.
caveats: Weekly is directional only (66-75 trades over 26 years, misses a cell in 3 of 5 variants) -- not run through the honest protocol.
Hourly has no data behind it yet (see above).
Not yet checked for monthly-R correlation against v5/v6/Logic 3 -- structurally close to Logic 3's double bottom, so it may not be as diversifying as it looks until that check runs.
Resistance is frozen at the ladder's highest pivot once armed; it does not ratchet up if a higher pivot prints during the 5-bar wait (unlike Logic 3's dynamic_ref) -- untested, not measured.
rejected: A volume filter on the breakout bar: -44% of trades for a worse CAGR (2.93% against 7.12%) -- the opposite of Logic 3, where volume helped.

rr_target, touch_atr and basis_slack_atr away from the chart's own defaults: each looked like an improvement in some single cut of the data and lost on the next one -- exactly what the honest protocol exists to catch.
The chart's literal 3-pivot ladder as a hard gate: only 9 trades in 26 years across 1,003 names -- real but too rare to filter on; better as a confidence tag on the 2-pivot signal.

strategies.name: MTF Trend Strategy
strategies.family: Monthly → Weekly → Daily trend alignment, ATR or swing-low exit
strategies.status_label: Scanned live from 2026-11-01, no live track record yet
strategies.universe: 986 names: 500 Nifty + 503 S&P 500 (the 17 dropped from 1,003 had under 260 bars of history)
strategies.headline: Started from a trader's own annotated chart screenshots (monthly key-level flip, weekly Fibonacci confluence, daily trendline break). Each visual rule was turned into an explicit, testable one, backtested on 26 years of data, then stress-tested with a 60-combination parameter sweep and a first-half-vs-second-half stability check before anything was scanned live.
entry: Monthly: close breaks above the trailing 12-month high, and that month's candle is bullish (close above open) and closes above the prior month's close -- the chart's 'key level resistance becomes support, with momentum'.

Weekly: close above a rising 20-week SMA, weekly RSI14 above 50, price pulled back into the 0.5-0.618 Fibonacci zone of the last 26-week swing within the last 6 weeks, and the latest completed weekly candle is bullish and closes in the top half of its range -- the chart's 'area of confluence'.

Daily: 3-bar fractal swing detection; the latest confirmed swing low is higher than the one before it AND the latest swing high is higher than the one before it (first higher-high/higher-low), and the close breaks above the swing high that defined the prior down-leg -- the chart's 'trendline broke'.

Entry is the next session's open, same convention as every other strategy here. The original chart also called for a 4H/1H entry trigger; this project has no intraday data, so two systematic daily-bar proxies were tested and the live scan carries both (see Exit).
exit: B (recommended, the one sized live): stop = 2.0 x ATR14, target = entry + 2.0 x stop. The center of a broad, stable plateau found by sweeping 10 ATR multipliers x 6 reward:risk ratios (60 combinations) -- avg R was within 0.6% between the first and second half of the 26-year backtest, and its India/US performance gap was the smallest of anything tested, meaning the edge isn't concentrated in one market.

A (shown alongside, not sized): stop = the lowest low of the trailing 3 days, target = entry + 3R. This is the single best full-sample number of everything tested (avg R +0.592, Calmar 109 against B's 94), but it decayed 8.6% between the first and second half of history and its win rate collapsed to 11.9% during its worst drawdown (the April-June 2010 Flash Crash window) -- more fragile under stress than B.

No trailing stop, break-even move or time stop beyond a 90-trading-day cutoff used only in the backtest. If one bar touches both stop and target, the stop is assumed. No commissions or slippage are modelled.
filters: No regime gate, position cap or risk throttle yet -- unlike v5/v6/logic3, nothing here limits how many of these signals could fire at once.

The backtest found this is exactly the open problem: up to 303 positions were open at the same time across the full signal set, and the single worst drawdown (Dec 2017-Mar 2018, -47.3R combined) lined up with the February 2018 volatility spike -- one correlated macro shock hitting many open positions together, not many independent bad picks. A concurrent-position cap and a losing-streak cooldown are the top candidates for a version 2.
strategies.verdict: Built and tested in one sitting on 2026-10-29/30: an 8,746-trade backtest (both daily-bar entry proxies, 2008 and 2020 excluded) showed a genuine, consistent edge (avg R +0.59, profit factor ~2.1, positive in all 9 market-and-entry slices and all 6 five-year periods). A parameter sweep across the user's own suggested change (replace the discretionary swing-low stop with a pure ATR-based stop and reward:risk target) found a broad, non-spiky plateau around ATR 2.0x-3.0x / RR 1.5-2.5 (Calmar 85-109) rather than one fragile peak, which is the main reason to trust it enough to scan live. The original swing-low approach (A) still has the better backtested number; the ATR approach (B) is the more mechanical, more stable one, which is why it is the one actually sized.
caveats: This is one objective reading of a trader's visual chart annotations ('area of confluence', 'candlestick patterns', 'trendline break'), not a transcription of exact discretionary judgment -- a different, equally reasonable coding of the same screenshots could score differently.

The daily-bar entry proxies (A and B) stand in for a 4H/1H entry this project cannot backtest or scan live -- there is no free intraday history going back to 2000, and the live scanner only ever sees end-of-day bars.

Survivorship bias on the US side: the S&P 500 sheet lists today's constituents, so delisted/acquired/bankrupt names are missing from the 2000s-2010s part of the backtest, which flatters the US numbers somewhat.

No position cap, correlation control or cost model yet (see Filters) -- the live scan can and will flag many names on the same day during a broad market uptrend, exactly the scenario that produced the worst backtested drawdowns.
No live track record. Watch it the way ema20confirm and v6 are being watched before sizing real money.
rejected: Stop = 1.25 x ATR14 + a flat 5-point add (the first version of the user's parameter idea): the flat points term is trivial on a $500 stock and catastrophic on a $6 one (split-adjusted history), pushing some stops to 99.7% of the entry price. Dropping the flat add fixed it completely (median stop fell from 9.4% to 2.9% of price).

The single best grid cell from the 60-combination sweep (ATR 2.0x / RR 2.5, Calmar 101): picking the literal best cell from an in-sample search with no out-of-sample test is exactly how a backtest gets curve-fit. The plateau's center (ATR 2.0x / RR 2.0) was chosen instead, and it is also the most stable of every config tested, which the single best cell was not.

Reporting drawdown from the first pass of the grid sweep: that version concatenated each symbol's trades in symbol order instead of sorting the whole trade list by actual date, which understated drawdown by up to 3x. Caught by spot-checking the top candidates against a correctly-dated recomputation before anything was trusted.

strategies.name: Master Support & Resistance Framework
strategies.family: 6-step, 100-point checklist scorer on three timeframe pairings (Hourly/Daily, Daily/Weekly, Weekly/Monthly)
strategies.status_label: Checklist scorer, not backtested -- track its score against real outcomes before trusting it
strategies.headline: Started from a trader's own written checklist (Support/Resistance quality, Market Bias, Area of Value, Confirmation pattern, Risk:Reward, Multi-timeframe Confluence -- each 0-15/0-20 points, 100 total, graded A+ to D) covering three named strategies: Hourly swing (2-10 days, entry on the hour, trend read from Daily), Daily positional (2-8 weeks, entry on the day, trend from Weekly), and Weekly position (2-12 months, entry on the week, trend from Monthly). Unlike every backtested strategy on this page, this one has not been tested against history at all yet -- it is a live mechanical scorer only, built to let the checklist run itself instead of being eyeballed chart by chart.
entry: Step 1 Support/Resistance (0/5/10/15): swing highs and lows (3-bar fractals) within 1.5% of each other are grouped into one zone; score comes from how many times that zone has been touched (2 touches = 5, 3-4 = 10, 5+ = 15).

Step 2 Market Bias (0/5/10/15): direction (bullish/bearish/neutral) from the literal checklist rule -- higher-high + higher-low vs lower-high + lower-low on the last two confirmed swings. Strength/quality is read from ADX(14) rather than eyeballed (sideways <15, weak 15-20, clear 20-30, strong 30+), since 'is the trend obvious' isn't otherwise mechanical. Neutral bias is a hard stop -- no direction means no trade, straight from the checklist's own Golden Rule.
Step 3 Area of Value (0/5/10/15): 0 if price sits away from any level, 5 within 3%, 10 on an actual touch, 15 if the latest bar both touched the zone and closed back away from it (a rejection wick).

Step 4 Confirmation (0/10/15/20): bullish/bearish engulfing, hammer/shooting star, a strong trend candle, an inside-bar breakout, and a same-direction double bottom/top are all checked on the latest bars; a double top/bottom alone scores 15, any single signal scores 10, a pattern plus a strong candle together scores 20.

Step 5 Risk:Reward (0/5/10/15): stop = nearest swing low/high in the trailing 10 bars, minus/plus 1x ATR(14) (exactly the checklist's formula). Target is the nearest opposing S&R zone if it clears 1.5R, otherwise a flat 2.5R projection. Scored 0 under 1.5R, 5 at 1.5R, 10 at 2.0R, 15 at 3.0R+.

Step 6 Multi-timeframe Confluence (0/10/20): compares this timeframe's bias against the next one up (Hourly checks Daily, Daily checks Weekly, Weekly checks Monthly when there's enough history -- Monthly is explicitly optional in the checklist). Same direction on both = 20, either side unclear or the higher timeframe unavailable = 10, opposite directions = 0.

A symbol only becomes a row in the live scan once its total clears that strategy's own minimum (Hourly 75+, Daily 80+, Weekly 85+, straight from the checklist) -- everything scored below that is computed but dropped, not shown as a weak signal.
exit: Stop and target come out of Step 5 above (ATR-based stop, nearest-opposing-zone-or-2.5R target) -- the same levels used to score Risk:Reward are the ones reported for the trade.
No trailing stop, break-even rule, or time stop -- the checklist doesn't specify one for this framework, unlike the position-sizing detail in some of the other strategies here.

Entry is approximated by the scanned bar's close, same convention used for display (not execution) elsewhere on this page -- the live scanner reports today's/this hour's/this week's setup, not a backtested fill.
filters: Three independent passes per symbol, not one: Hourly uses 60-minute bars (Yahoo only keeps ~730 days of those) with the Daily chart as its higher timeframe; Daily and Weekly share one ~5-year daily fetch, with Weekly and Monthly built locally by resampling it.
No regime gate, position cap, correlation control, or cost model of any kind -- this is a per-symbol checklist score, nothing portfolio-level.
Scheduled alongside the MTF scan -- see scan_US.bat / scan_India.bat in MSR_Strategy/. Writes LATEST_MSR_<market>.json (three strategies in one file) and a dated three-sheet Excel archive.
strategies.verdict: Built 2026-11-01 directly from the trader's own 6-step scoring table and three strategy definitions, pasted in full. This is the one strategy on this page shipped with ZERO backtest -- every other live scanner here (MTF, Weinstein, dbpyramid, etc.) went through a historical validation pass first; this one didn't, because the checklist as written is a discretionary scoring rubric, not a single testable entry/exit rule, and turning six judgment calls into six formulas (documented in msr_core.py's own docstring) is itself the thing that needs checking against outcomes before it's trusted. Treat every row as 'the checklist's own math says this', not as a proven edge.
caveats: Not backtested. No win rate, profit factor, or drawdown number exists for this strategy and none should be assumed -- that is exactly the gap the Suggested improvements note below exists to close.

Several of the checklist's own scoring inputs aren't fully mechanical in the original text (e.g. 'strong rejection zone', 'is the trend obvious') -- the coded version makes a specific, documented choice for each (see msr_core.py's docstring), and a different reasonable reading of the same checklist could score differently, same caveat as the MTF strategy above.

The Hourly strategy's higher-timeframe check (Daily) and the Weekly strategy's (Monthly, when available) only compare DIRECTION, not strength -- two markets with the same bias but very different trend quality score the same on Step 6.

Fixed 1.5% zone-clustering tolerance and 3-bar fractal window are shared across all three timeframes (hours, days, weeks) for simplicity; a tolerance tuned per timeframe would likely group zones more sensibly, especially on the Weekly chart.
No position sizing, portfolio cap, or regime filter -- same gap as the MTF strategy, not yet addressed here either.

strategies.name: Double-bottom pyramid (RSI divergence + trendline + EMA20 + breakout + retest)
strategies.family: Scaled-in reversal: EMA20 reclaim, then confirmed breakout, then a held retest
strategies.status_label: Backtested 2026-10-31, scanned live from 2026-11-01, no live track record yet
strategies.headline: Started from a trader's own 6-step annotated chart (RSI divergence, a double bottom or inverse head-and-shoulders, a broken descending trendline, an EMA20 reclaim, a break of structure, then a breakout-and-retest), coded into exact rules, backtested on 26 years of daily EOD data, then live-scanned daily. The backtest's own biggest finding: the first tranche alone is a false start two-thirds of the time -- see Verdict.
entry: Pattern: two swing lows (3-bar fractal) 10-180 bars apart, the second within -15%/+4% of the first, separated by a base peak at least 8% above the first low.
Filter 1, RSI divergence: RSI14 at the second low is higher than RSI14 at the first low (classic bullish divergence).

Filter 2, trendline break: close above the line connecting the swing high before the first low and the base peak, when that line is descending (if no such line exists, this filter is skipped for that pattern).
Tranche 1 (25%): first close above the 20 EMA at or after the trendline break.
Tranche 2 (25%): first close above the base peak after tranche 1 fires -- the chart's 'close above previous LH and make HH'.
Tranche 3 (50%): after tranche 2, price pulls back to within 3% of the base peak and closes back above it within 5 bars -- the chart's 'breakout and retrace at same level'.

Live scanner only surfaces a pattern whose tranche-1 EMA reclaim happened in the last 20 trading days, and drops it the moment the stop is breached, so the page never shows a stale or already-invalidated setup.
exit: Stop: 1% below the second swing low. Trades where that stop is under 2% of the entry price are skipped entirely -- a sub-2% stop is a real risk-sizing problem, not just a backtest edge case: the first version of this backtest let a handful of these through, and the resulting divide-by-near-zero R-multiples (one hit +128R) accounted for more than 100% of the whole backtest's reported profit before the floor was added.
Target: the base peak plus the pattern's own height (peak minus first low), the standard double-bottom measured move.
Time stop: 252 trading bars. No break-even move, trail or scale-out modelled.
No commissions or slippage modelled.
filters: 2008 and 2020 excluded from the backtest by request (crisis years treated as outliers, not representative of normal conditions).
One position per symbol; no portfolio cap, regime gate or risk throttle yet -- unlike v5/v6/logic3, nothing here limits how many of these could fire at once.

The live scanner uses yfinance split/dividend-adjusted prices; the backtest used raw (unadjusted) Close/High/Low with a same-day >50% move filter to catch bad prints, so a handful of backtested Indian-market patterns may be bonus-issue artifacts that the live scanner, on adjusted data, will not reproduce.
strategies.verdict: 886 trades, 2000-2026 ex 2008/2020, 1,003 names: win rate 50.2%, avg R +0.07, profit factor 1.14 -- barely better than breakeven taken as specified, and in India the lifetime drawdown (-52R) dwarfs the lifetime gain (+12R). But splitting by how far each pattern actually got changes the picture completely: patterns that stalled at tranche 1 (33% of all setups, EMA reclaim only, breakout never came) won just 6.4% of the time at -0.52R average -- pure value destruction. Patterns that reached a confirmed breakout (tranche 2 or 3, 67% of setups) won 72.1% of the time at +0.365R average, profit factor 2.36. Treating the EMA reclaim as a watch-alert rather than a funded entry, and only sizing once the breakout confirms, is therefore the single highest-leverage change to this strategy. A second finding: the edge is heavily front-loaded -- pre-2018 confirmed-breakout trades scored +0.40R (PF 2.58); 2018-2026 confirmed-breakout trades scored only +0.10R (PF 1.25) overall, and were a net loser in the US subsample alone (avg R -0.11, PF 0.80, n=22 -- a small sample, a warning sign rather than proof).
caveats: No walk-forward or train/test split was run -- unlike v5/v6/logic3/mtf, this has not been through the full honest protocol yet (select on early years, confirm once on held-out later years never touched during selection).

The exit rules (stop/target/time-stop) were not specified by the original chart annotations and were chosen by whoever coded this -- a different, equally reasonable choice of exits could score differently.

The retest requirement (tranche 3) adds only a little over just trading the confirmed breakout alone (+0.38R blended full-pyramid vs +0.16R breakout-only-no-retest in the raw trade split) -- decide deliberately whether waiting for it is worth missing fast breakouts that never pull back.

Post-2018 performance, especially in the US, is materially weaker than the lifetime average and should not be assumed to carry forward; re-validate on a rolling recent window before sizing real money.
No live track record yet. Watch it the way ema20confirm, v6 and the MTF strategy are being watched before sizing real money.
rejected: Trusting the first run's headline number (avg R +0.25, looked profitable): 6 of 927 trades had a stop sitting within 2% (one within 0.1%) of entry, blowing their R-multiples up to +18R/+30R/+128R; those 6 trades alone summed to more than the entire backtest's total profit. Rejected in favor of a hard minimum-stop-distance floor (see Exit), after which the honest number is +0.07R, not +0.25R.

Sizing tranche-1-only trades at their nominal 25% weight: for R-multiple comparability every trade in this backtest is renormalized to 100% of whatever tranches actually filled, so a tranche-1-only trade's -0.52R average overstates its real portfolio impact (it was only ever a 25% position) -- a straight read of the Verdict's numbers should account for that before concluding tranche 1 alone is this costly in real equity terms.
