strategies.name: EMA-VCP Positional Strategy
strategies.family: Weekly -> Daily -> Hourly VCP (volatility contraction pattern), EMA-anchored trade management
strategies.status_label: Backtested and threshold-swept on 26 years; scanned live from 2026-11-01, no live track record yet
strategies.universe: 986 names: 500 Nifty + 503 S&P 500 (same universe as the MTF Trend Strategy)
strategies.headline: Started from a trader-pasted VCP checklist (Weekly -> Daily -> Hourly multi-timeframe scorecard, 110 points, Elite/A+/B/Watchlist/Reject grading) with every checkbox turned into an explicit formula. Running the checklist's own literal thresholds produced only 16 trades across the whole 26-year universe -- too few to mean anything -- so a threshold sweep was run before anything shipped live. The sweep found the checklist's own Daily-Structure-score gate (>=15/20) is a cliff where the edge collapses outright, not a safety margin; lowering it to >=10 with the breakout-volume requirement at 1.25x (down from the checklist's 1.4x) restores a statistically solid result while keeping the Weekly/Volume/Hourly gates at the checklist's own literal numbers, which tested fine as written.
entry: Weekly VCP Analysis (score >=30/40): price above a rising 30-week MA, higher weekly highs and lows, a relative-strength line making new highs against an equal-weight universe benchmark, tight weekly candles with volume drying up -- no market-cap index exists in this project, so RS and the Market Filter below both use the same equal-weight synthetic index + breadth already built for the other strategies here.

Daily VCP Structure (score >=10/20, lowered from the checklist's own >=15 -- see headline): a base 4-20 weeks old, 3+ progressively smaller contractions, the final one <=5%, volatility (ATR%) trending down.

Volume Dry-Up (score >=10/15) and Breakout (pivot clarity + volume >=1.25x the 50-day average, close above the base's high): the final contraction's own volume well below average, then a real expansion on the breakout bar.

Hourly Precision Entry (score >=10/15): on real data this needs intraday bars; the live scanner uses a daily-bar VWAP/EMA20 proxy for now (another strategy on this page, Pullback-Retest MTF, already proved real 60-minute Yahoo bars are available live -- upgrading this strategy's Hourly leg to real hourly data is the next concrete step, not yet done).

Market Filter: universe breadth (% of names above their own 200-day SMA) > 40%, same house threshold used elsewhere on this page -- no real S&P500/Nifty500 index is cached in this project to check directly.
exit: Stop = the lower of the final contraction's low and the breakout candle's low.
Scale out 25% at +10%, 25% at +20%, trail the remaining 50% on the 21-day EMA once both partials are taken; hard stop throughout.
Also exits on two consecutive daily closes below the 21 EMA.
filters: Market breadth > 40%.
Risk (entry to stop) under 8% of entry price.
strategies.verdict: 134 trades over 26 years (about 5/year across both markets combined), 48.5% win rate, avg R +0.64, profit factor 2.24, t=3.46 -- a real, if infrequent, signal at the swept thresholds. The checklist's own exact Daily-Structure threshold is actively harmful (t collapses to 0.1-1.6 at >=15 across every breakout-volume setting tested), which is the headline finding of the whole exercise: formalizing a discretionary checklist into exact numbers is only useful if each number then gets checked against history, not assumed correct because it came from an experienced trader's own notes.
caveats: No real hourly data backs the Hourly leg -- a daily-bar proxy stands in for it, same caveat as MTF's 4H/1H leg.
The Market Filter and Strategy 1's relative-strength line both use an equal-weight synthetic index built from this project's own universe, not a real market-cap index -- there is none cached here.
Only the Daily Structure x breakout-volume gate (2 of 5 dimensions) was swept on a grid; Weekly/Volume/Hourly minimums were only spot-checked, not swept as finely.
A concurrency cap (20 open positions) paradoxically worsened this backtest's realized drawdown rather than improving it, most likely a small-sample trade-ordering artifact -- flagged, not resolved.
rejected: The checklist's own literal Daily Structure score minimum (>=15/20) -- empirically destroys the edge rather than protecting it.

strategies.name: Pullback-Retest MTF Swing Strategy
strategies.family: Weekly -> Daily -> Hourly pullback/retest/entry, each on its own 100-point scorecard, plus a 100-point alignment model that sets position size
strategies.status_label: Weekly+Daily backtested on 26 years; scanned live from 2026-11-01 using REAL hourly bars, no live track record yet
strategies.headline: Started from a trader-supplied 6-stage pullback/retest/entry framework pasted in full, run independently on Weekly, Daily and Hourly bars with its own 100-point scorecard per timeframe, plus a separate Multi-Timeframe Alignment Model (100 pts) that sizes the trade in R. The live scanner uses real hourly bars (not a daily-bar proxy), since free Yahoo data covers about 2 years of 60-minute bars -- more than this strategy's own 1-10 day hourly holding period needs.
entry: Stage 1 Trend filter (per timeframe): close above (long) / below (short) a 50-EMA that is itself rising/falling, plus a confirmed higher-high+higher-low (long) or lower-high+lower-low (short) from 3-bar fractal swings. Neither -> no trade on that timeframe.

Stage 2 Pullback: a fresh confirmed swing high (long) / low (short) that is itself a new extreme anchors the pullback. From there, 2+ consecutive candles against the trend must follow, with the pullback staying on the correct side of the confirmed swing before the anchor (the major structure level).
Stage 3 Retest zone: once the pullback ends, its own extreme becomes the retest zone -- price must revisit it (within 1%) and the zone must hold.
Stage 4 Entry trigger: the first candle back in the trend's direction that closes beyond the high/low of the most recent counter-trend candle, after the retest holds. Enter at the next bar's open.

Weekly Position scorecard (100 pts, 3-12 month hold): EMA/trend (20), HH-HL (20), base breakout (15), pullback length 2-5 candles (10), retest holds (15), reversal candle at support (10), volume expansion (10).
Daily Swing scorecard (100 pts, 1-8 week hold): daily trend (20), weekly aligned (15), fresh swing (15), 2+ candle pullback (10), volume dry-up (10), retest holds (15), trigger candle (15).

Hourly Swing scorecard (100 pts, 1-10 day hold): daily trend (20), hourly trend (15), hourly HH-HL (15), 2+ candle pullback (10), retest tested (15), reversal candle (15), real RR >= 2:1 against the nearest structural target (10).

Multi-Timeframe Alignment Model (100 pts): Weekly uptrend (35), Daily uptrend + active pullback (30), Hourly trigger fired (20), volume expansion (10), RR >= 2 (5). Final Rule: only take a trade at alignment >= 85 AND all three timeframes agreed AND the hourly trigger fires on the latest bar -- the checklist's own claim is this removes 70-80% of low-quality setups.
exit: Stop = the pullback/structure level minus (long) / plus (short) 1x ATR(14), moved to breakeven the first time the trade reaches +1R.

T1 = 1.5R, close 50%. T2 = 2.0R, close 25%. Remaining 25% runs to T3 (the prior opposing swing high/low) or exits on a close back across the 50-EMA, or a 40-trading-day time stop (the checklist's own 1-8 week daily holding period), whichever comes first.
Position size from the Alignment Model's score: 90-100 -> 1.0R, 80-89 -> 0.75R, 70-79 -> 0.5R, under 70 -> no trade.
filters: Backtest covers Weekly+Daily only (both directions), 2000-2026, 2008 and 2020 excluded -- this project has no free intraday history back to 2000, so the Hourly layer (which carries its own full scorecard and entry trigger, unlike MTF/EMA Positional's intraday layers which are pure entry-timing) is dropped rather than faked with a daily-bar proxy.

The short side is DISABLED in the live scanner (ALLOW_SHORT = False in pbmtf_scan.py): the backtest found it loses money outright (40 trades, 25% win rate, avg R -0.42, profit factor 0.34) while longs carry the whole edge.
No concurrent-position cap, correlation control or liquidity filter -- same open gap as every other strategy on this page.
strategies.verdict: Built 2026-11-01 directly from the trader's own pasted 6-stage framework and three scorecards. The Weekly+Daily mechanics have a real, positive, consistent edge in both markets (avg R +0.09 to +0.14, profit factor 1.26-1.44) -- entirely on the long side. Two real bugs were found and fixed while building this: a tautological Risk:Reward check (comparing price to a target that is always exactly 2R by construction, so it could never fail) was rewritten to grade against the real nearest structural target instead; and a one-bar lookahead in how a 3-bar fractal swing becomes "known" (shared by this project's MTF, EMA Positional and MSR strategies) was fixed here and flagged for backporting.
caveats: The Hourly layer's contribution to the Multi-Timeframe Alignment Model has not been walk-forward tested over any meaningful history -- free hourly data only goes back about 2 years. Treat the backtest numbers above as validating the Weekly+Daily mechanics only; the live scanner's three-way-aligned signal is unproven beyond what accumulates from here forward.
Short side disabled by default after the backtest showed it loses money -- do not re-enable it without a market-level regime filter or a rebuild.

"Strong breakout from base" and the candlestick/volume checks are this project's own systematized reading of visual checklist items, not a literal transcription -- see PBMTF_STRATEGY_SPEC.md for every one.
India's EOD archive has patchy/zero Volume data for smaller Nifty 500 names, especially pre-2010 -- every volume-based check silently scores false rather than erroring when that happens.
No concurrent-position cap or losing-streak cooldown -- pullback-continuation setups are exactly the kind that cluster in a single correlated market move.

strategies.name: Break & Retest Master Framework
strategies.family: C.E.S.T model (Conditions / Entry / Stop / Target), 100-point scorer on three timeframe pairings
strategies.status_label: Daily and Weekly backtested and scanned live from 2026-11-01; Hourly is live-only, no live track record yet
strategies.headline: Started from a trader's own 'C.E.S.T' write-up and its 100-point scoring rubric, covering three named strategies: Hourly swing (2-10 days), Daily positional (2 weeks-3 months) and Weekly position (1-12 months). One of three chart patterns must exist (trend-continuation break, consolidation-range break, or triangle break), each followed by a retest of the broken level and a rejection candle, scored across five sections (Trend Quality, Breakout Quality, Retest Quality, Multi-Timeframe Alignment, Risk:Reward) for a 0-100 total. Daily and Weekly were backtested on 26 years of daily EOD data (the Weekly strategy simulated on daily bars so a stop can't be blurred through mid-week); Hourly has no free source of 60-minute bars going back further than about 2 years, so it is live-only -- see Caveats.
entry: Conditions (one of three): Pattern 1 Trend Continuation -- an uptrend (confirmed higher-high/higher-low swing structure) breaks its most recent swing high (downtrend/swing-low break for shorts). Pattern 2 Consolidation -- a tight multi-bar range with 2+ touches of both edges, broken by a strong-bodied candle. Pattern 3 Triangle -- a rising triangle (flat resistance, rising swing lows) breaking up, or a falling triangle breaking down.

Retest -- within a timeframe-sized window of bars after the break, price must return to within a small ATR-based tolerance of the broken level without re-breaking the structure behind the move, then show a rejection candle (hammer/pin bar/engulfing/strong close).

Entry Level 1 (Aggressive): right at the retest touch. Level 2 (Conservative): on the rejection candle's own close -- the level this framework's signal actually fires on. Level 3 (Professional) is Section D's multi-timeframe alignment scoring full marks, not a separate rule.

Hourly strategy adds: Weekly trend agrees, Daily is above/below its 20-EMA in the trade direction, volume expands on the 1H breakout. Daily strategy adds: Weekly trend agrees, Daily's own HH-HL structure agrees, and a next-bar follow-through close stands in for the doc's '4H reversal pattern' (no 26-year 4H archive to backtest against -- see Caveats). Weekly strategy adds: price above its rolling 30-week MA, Daily confirms the same direction.
exit: Stop: below the retest low or the swing low behind the whole move, whichever is lower (mirrored for shorts) -- exactly the doc's own rule.

Target: never less than 1.5R; uses the next major structural level (a rolling high/low over a longer lookback, standing in for 'previous resistance / weekly resistance') when that reaches further than 2R, otherwise a flat 2R.

Entry for the backtest/live fill is the next bar's open on that same timeframe (this project's universal convention). If one bar's range contains both the stop and the target, the stop is assumed. No commissions or slippage modelled.
filters: Score gate per strategy, straight from the doc's own checklists: Hourly needs the total score at or above 80, Daily at or above 85, Weekly at or above 90 -- the strictest of the three, matching the doc calling the weekly setup 'the highest probability'.

No concurrent-position cap or losing-streak cooldown yet -- same open problem MTF_STRATEGY_SPEC.md already found for its own strategy: a correlated macro shock can hit many open positions from this framework at once, not many independent bad picks.
strategies.verdict: Full-universe backtest (1,003 symbols, 2001-2026, 2008/2020 excluded), simulated on daily bars for both: Daily strategy 3,180 trades, 43.7% win rate, avg R +0.294, profit factor 1.53, total +933.7R, max drawdown -50.4R, Calmar 18.5. Weekly strategy 1,725 trades, 49.9% win rate, avg R +0.238, profit factor 1.58, total +410.0R, max drawdown -60.3R, Calmar 6.8. Both net positive, and India outperformed the US on every metric for both strategies -- the same ranking MTF_STRATEGY_SPEC.md found independently for an unrelated strategy, which makes it look like a structural fact about these two markets rather than a coincidence of this framework. Weekly's win rate and profit factor beat Daily's, matching the original doc's own claim that the weekly setup is the highest-probability of the three -- but Weekly's max drawdown is actually worse than Daily's despite that, a sign of the same correlated-position risk noted in Filters. One literal reading of the Weekly checklist ('3R minimum' AND 'highest volume in 8-12 weeks', both hard-gated at their strictest wording) produced zero signals in 24 years on a sample test -- both were relaxed to be scored, not separately hard-gated, which is what actually produced the numbers above; see the full spec for why.
caveats: No free source of 60-minute (or 4-hour) bars going back further than about 2 years (yfinance's own limit) -- the Hourly strategy, and the Daily strategy's '4H reversal pattern' checklist item, cannot be backtested over this project's full 2001-2026 window the way Daily and Weekly were. Both use a systematic daily-bar proxy where a true intraday backtest isn't possible, the same kind of substitution MTF_Strategy and EMA_Positional_Strategy already made for their own intraday layers.

'Obvious to everyone' (breakout clarity), triangle flat-vs-sloped, and 'strong/neutral/against' trend are all discretionary chart-reading calls in the original doc, turned into explicit ATR-relative and regression-slope rules here -- a different, equally reasonable coding of the same wording could score differently.

The Weekly strategy's '3R minimum' and 'highest volume in 8-12 weeks' checklist items are scored (feeding the 0-100 total) rather than separately hard-gated at their strictest literal reading, because hard-gating both at once produced zero trades in 24 years -- see Verdict.

Section D (Multi-Timeframe Alignment) substantially re-measures the same trend agreement Section A already scores, just packaged differently -- 40 of the 100 points are not fully independent information.

No position sizing, concurrent-position cap, or out-of-sample (train/test split) stability check yet -- unlike MTF_Strategy and EMA_Positional_Strategy, which were both stress-tested before being sized. Treat the backtest numbers above as 'the logic is sound and net positive', not 'these exact parameters are optimal'.
rejected: Hard-gating the Weekly strategy's '3R minimum' (rr_score >= 15) together with its volume item at the strictest literal reading (volume_expansion_score >= 10): produced zero signals across a 60-symbol-per-market sample over 24 years. Relaxed both to feed the score instead of double-hard-gating, which is what produced a believable ~200-trade result.

strategies.name: Inverse head & shoulders
strategies.family: Reversal pattern: LS/head/RS swing lows, neckline break, retest or breakout entry
strategies.status_label: First pass, narrow edge, US only
strategies.headline: Classic three-swing-low reversal pattern (left shoulder, a deeper head, a right shoulder) that breaks back above the neckline through the two bounces between them. Two entry styles were tested: buy the breakout itself, or wait for price to come back and hold the neckline first. No single configuration wins everywhere -- the two validated results are both in the US; nothing tested makes India reliably work.
entry: Three consecutive confirmed swing lows (left shoulder, head, right shoulder), the head strictly the deepest, shoulders within 1.5x ATR14 of each other in price and inside a loose time-symmetry band.

Neckline = the higher of the two reaction highs between the shoulders and the head (a flat line, not sloped -- a sloped neckline extrapolated forward was tried first and rejected for producing unstable targets).
Breakout entry: next bar's open after a green candle closes back above the neckline on at least 1.3x average volume, closing in the top 40% of its own range.

Retest entry (the better of the two styles in 3 of 4 cells, after a bug that inflated early results was found and fixed -- see caveats): instead of buying the breakout bar, wait for price to pull back to the neckline within 1%, hold a reclaim close back above it, then buy the next bar's open. Stop is the retest bar's own low, rejected if that stop is under 0.5% of price (too close to be a real risk-defined level).

The one filter that helped almost everywhere: requiring rolling-average volume to strictly decline left-shoulder to head to right-shoulder (volume drying up ahead of the breakout). Requiring the US daily setup's weekly chart to also be constructive (classify_context() on the weekly-resampled series) helped US daily specifically but hurt India daily when added to the same stack.
exit: Target: the classic measured move -- neckline value at confirmation plus the vertical drop from neckline to head.
Breakout-style stop: the right shoulder's own low, no buffer.
Retest-style stop: the retest bar's own low (tighter, but only usable once the minimum-risk check passes).

A close back below the neckline after confirmation (a failed reclaim) exits regardless of the nominal stop -- this is the single biggest failure mode of the breakout style, 39-61% of confirmed patterns even after every filter tested.
filters: A downtrend-context gate (reusing market_context.py, read at either the left or right shoulder) was tested and does not help -- flat to slightly negative at both anchors, settled as a closed question rather than left open.
A pattern-height floor (1x ATR14) was tested and has no effect -- it almost never binds once the shoulder/time-symmetry checks already applied have run.

RSI bullish divergence at the head was tested and hurts, consistently, in every one of 8 comparisons across both entry styles -- the shoulder-symmetry rule already favors fast moves where momentum often hasn't diverged yet.

A 2-bar hold requirement on the breakout (the close must stay above the neckline a second bar, not just one) helps the base pattern modestly and rescues the one weak India-weekly cell when stacked with retest entry, but costs the best India-daily result when stacked the same way -- not a free add-on.

Runs daily in scan_US.bat / scan_India.bat, surfacing only live setups (forming, awaiting a retest/reclaim, or an open trade) using the best validated config per market and timeframe, not a historical dump. Writes LATEST_INVERSEHS_<market>.json.
strategies.verdict: 26-year backtest (2000-2026, 2008/2020 excluded), 1,003 names, pooled trade-level stats. Every suggestion from the original spec was tested: context gate (both anchors), 2-bar confirmation, height floor, RSI divergence, volume shape, retest entry, and nested weekly-context gating, alone and in combination. The two results that actually clear this project's own v5/v6 bar (avg R 0.25-0.34): US weekly with retest entry + volume shape (+0.281R blended) and US daily with retest entry + volume shape + weekly context (+0.172R, smaller sample). India's best anywhere is daily retest entry + volume shape alone (+0.108R) -- every further filter stacked on top made India worse, not better, four separate times, which looks like a real market difference rather than noise, though the mechanism isn't identified.
caveats: A real bug was found and fixed mid-project: the retest-entry stop had no minimum-risk floor (unlike analog_setup.py's own backtest_retest(), which it was modeled on), so a handful of near-zero-risk trades produced 50-200x R-multiple outliers that inflated several early results, India daily most of all (originally reported as high as +0.258R, corrected to +0.040-0.108R depending on configuration). All affected numbers were re-run and corrected; the figures above are post-fix.
No train/test split -- this is one 26-year sample, not validated the way v5/v6/logic3 went through a select-early/confirm-late protocol.
The US daily result (retest + volume shape + weekly context) ran on a few hundred trades, smaller than most other cells here -- hold it a little more loosely than the US weekly result.
Hourly was never implemented: this project has no intraday data pipeline, and free sources only cover 60-730 days, far short of what a pattern that can take months to form needs.

Live scanning only surfaces the single most recent swing-low triple per symbol per timeframe (same convention as the analog setup scanner), using the per-cell config above -- not a blend or a vote across configs.
rejected: A sloped neckline through the two reaction highs, extrapolated forward: unstable, could put the target below entry on a steep slope (caught via a negative-R target exit in testing).
Downtrend-context gate at either shoulder: flat to slightly negative, inside the same noise band at both anchors.
RSI bullish divergence at the head, with either entry style: hurts in all 8 comparisons tested.
Pattern-height floor at 1x ATR14: no measurable effect, removes under 0.4% of patterns anywhere.

strategies.name: Fundamental Analysis Master Framework
strategies.family: 6-stage fundamentals scorer: business quality, industry rank, valuation, forward earnings, catalysts, red flags
strategies.status_label: Checklist scorer on financial statements, not backtested -- track its grades against real outcomes before trusting it
strategies.universe: StockLens's own watchlist only (8 US + 4 NSE names), NOT the 1,003-name universe every other strategy here scans
strategies.headline: A pasted fundamentals rubric (Revenue/EPS growth, margin trend, ROIC, debt, industry leadership, PEG, margin-of-safety DCF discount, forward EPS growth, catalysts, a 10-item red-flag checklist) turned into Quality (0-100) and Opportunity (0-100) scores, blended 60/40 into an Investment Score and an A+-D grade, plus a Minervini-style weekly/daily technical-confirmation layer. Runs inside the StockLens app (G:\STOCK) against its own tracked watchlist, not this project's 1,003-name price universe, because fundamentals need several separate Yahoo Finance calls per symbol (statements, not one batched OHLCV call) -- scanning 1,003 names for fundamentals daily would be slow and likely to trip Yahoo's rate limiter for data that doesn't change daily the way prices do.
entry: Quality (0-100): Growth 25pts (5yr-or-best-available revenue + EPS CAGR, banded), Margins 15pts (gross+operating trend), ROIC 15pts, Balance Sheet 10pts (debt/equity banded), Industry Position 20pts (this symbol's growth/margin/ROIC percentile against every OTHER symbol scanned this run in the same Yahoo sector -- a real cross-sectional rank, just over a small peer group), Management 15pts (buyback/no-dilution + ROIC>WACC + gross-margin level as a capital-allocation/moat proxy).

Opportunity (0-100): Valuation 40pts (PEG banded + DCF-intrinsic-value discount to price, DCF reused from StockLens's own fundamentals engine), Forecast Growth 40pts (forward EPS growth estimate, else the DCF's own growth path, else historical EPS CAGR), Catalysts 20pts across 4 signals worth 5pts each -- all computable from statements/quotes, substituted for the original rubric's news-driven catalysts (new product, new management): sector-tailwind keyword match, operating-margin-expansion trend, EPS growth accelerating YoY, forward PE below trailing PE.

Investment Score = Quality x 60% + Opportunity x 40%. Grade: 90+ A+, 80+ A, 70+ B, 60+ C, else D. A category with zero data this run is dropped from that score's weighting rather than scored as 0, so a stock isn't punished for a statement line Yahoo doesn't carry.

Red flags (7 of the original 10 are computable: revenue/EPS declining, negative FCF, rising debt, share dilution, falling ROIC, margin compression; insider selling, guidance cuts and auditor concerns are NOT computable from statements and are explicitly excluded from the count rather than assumed clean) -- 3+ triggered sets reject=true.

Phase-4 technical confirmation (weekly price/30-week-MA + MA slope, a momentum proxy for RS line, and four daily heuristics -- Bollinger-bandwidth contraction standing in for a real VCP detector, plus the existing 20-day volume ratio for dry/breakout volume) scores 0-100; the framework's own buy rule (fundamentals grade A/A+ AND technical score > 80) is reported per symbol as finalBuy.
exit: No stop/target/exit rule -- this is a fundamentals grade and a position-sizing suggestion (risk % and portfolio allocation %, straight from the pasted framework's own A+/A/B bands), not a timed trade signal like the price-based strategies on this page.
filters: Runs inside StockLens's own backend (app/analysis/master_framework.py), not as a standalone script against eod_cache.pkl like the other live scanners here -- MasterFramework_Strategy/master_framework_scan.py imports that app directly and reuses its tested scoring code rather than re-implementing it.

Scheduled as 'MasterFramework Scan_US' (07:00 SGT) and 'MasterFramework Scan_India' (19:00 SGT) daily, both calling the SAME underlying watchlist scan and filtering by exchange -- the India run mostly hits StockLens's own 24h fundamentals cache the US run already warmed. Writes LATEST_MASTERFRAMEWORK_<market>.json.

Industry Position and the sector-average-PE check are only as good as how many watchlist symbols share that sector this run -- with under 3 peers in a sector it degrades to 'not ranked' rather than guessing.
strategies.verdict: Built 2026-11-02 from a pasted 'FUNDAMENTAL ANALYSIS MASTER FRAMEWORK' scoring rubric (Quality/Opportunity categories, grading table, red-flag checklist, position-sizing table). Unlike every price-based strategy on this page, there is no trade log or R-multiple here to validate against -- it's a financial-statement scorer, and the only thing tested so far is that the arithmetic matches the rubric's own bands (5 unit tests against synthetic good/bad-company fixtures) and that it runs cleanly end-to-end against the real watchlist. One real bug was caught building it: Yahoo's annual-statement window sometimes has a trailing all-null fiscal year at the oldest edge (confirmed on NVDA), which silently zeroed the entire 25-point growth category before the CAGR calculation was fixed to walk back to the oldest NON-null year instead of blindly indexing the last column.
caveats: Not backtested, same caveat as MSR above -- no win rate or forward-return number exists for these grades yet.

Scans a 12-symbol watchlist, not the 1,003-name universe -- Industry Position and sector-average-PE are real cross-sectional comparisons, just over a much smaller and less representative peer set than a proper industry benchmark.

3 of the pasted framework's 10 red flags (insider selling, management lowering guidance, auditor concerns) aren't computable from Yahoo's financial statements and are excluded from the reject count, not treated as 'not triggered' -- a stock can still be hiding one of these three.

Stage-5 catalysts substitute 4 computable statement/quote signals for the original rubric's genuinely qualitative ones (new product cycle, new management, industry tailwind as written, margin expansion) -- a real news-driven catalyst can be happening and still score 0 here.

Phase-4 'VCP pattern' and 'tight consolidation' are a Bollinger-bandwidth-contraction proxy, not real pattern recognition -- flagged as a heuristic in the code and should be read as a rough stand-in, not a true VCP detector like the EMA-VCP strategy above (which also only approximates VCP, but with more structure).

Capital-allocation/moat scoring (Management, 15pts) is the weakest sub-score in the rubric -- buybacks + ROIC>WACC + gross-margin level is a coarse proxy for something that usually needs a human analyst's read.

strategies.family: 5-step 100-point checklist: Industry, Business Quality, Valuation, Supply/Demand, VCP Technical
strategies.status_label: Checklist scorer on financial statements + price action, not backtested -- track its grades against real outcomes before trusting it
strategies.universe: 503 US + 500 India names, same watchlist as the EMA-VCP scanner
strategies.headline: A pasted 'Akshat Shrivastava fundamental investing framework' checklist, scored end to end: Industry (25pts: growth potential, government-support themes, competitive intensity), Business Quality (30pts: ROCE, revenue/profit CAGR, debt/equity, promoter holding, cash flow), Valuation (20pts: PE vs sector, PEG, margin of safety against a Graham-formula intrinsic value), Supply/Demand (15pts: relative strength vs the benchmark index, institutional-holding level, an OBV-slope volume-accumulation proxy), and VCP Technical (10pts, reusing the EMA-VCP scanner's own contraction/volume-dry-up detector). Totals to a 100-point Decision Matrix (A+/A/B/Watchlist/Reject), a Trade Execution Checklist, position sizing by grade, and an Exit Framework (stop at the lower of the final contraction low or the 10-week MA, partial profit at +20%/+40%).
entry: Fundamental gate: Industry score >=18/25, Business Quality score >=22/30, Valuation score >=12/20 -- all three must pass.

Technical gate: close above both the 50-day and 200-day moving averages, a VCP base present (contraction legs tightening, final leg <=5%), relative strength strong versus the benchmark index, some volume dry-up in the final leg, and a breakout day with volume >=150% of the 50-day average.
Entry trigger: price closes above the VCP pivot, volume confirms (>1.5x the 50-day average), and the benchmark index itself is bullish (above its own rising 50/200-day average).
exit: Stop: the lower of the final VCP contraction leg's low or the 10-week moving average.
Partial profit: sell 25% at +20%, another 25% at +40%.

Final exit on any of: the 10-week MA breaking, a heavy-distribution-volume day, next-quarter fundamental deterioration (flagged for manual review -- not automatable from free annual-only statements), or relative strength weakening run-over-run.
filters: Position sizing by grade: A+ risks 1.5% of portfolio / 15-20% capital allocation, A risks 1.0% / 10-15%, B risks 0.5% / 5-10% -- straight from the pasted framework's own table.
Scheduled as 'Akshat Scan_US' (07:00 SGT) and 'Akshat Scan_India' (19:00 SGT) daily, in Fundamental_Scanner/akshat_scan.py. Writes LATEST_AKSHAT_<market>.json.
Fundamentals are cached 7 days (ROCE/debt/promoter-holding don't move day to day); price bars and the benchmark index are fetched live every run.
strategies.verdict: Built 2026-11-01/02 from a pasted 5-step scoring checklist attributed to Akshat Shrivastava, combined with this project's own EMA-VCP contraction detector for the technical leg. Two of the checklist's own sub-score groups didn't sum to their stated step maximum as written (Industry's three factors summed to 15, not the stated 25; Valuation's three summed to 15, not 20) and were rescaled proportionally rather than left to silently cap every score short of its band. Like Fundamental Analysis Master Framework above, there is no trade log or R-multiple here -- only that the scanner runs cleanly end to end against the full 1,003-name universe and that a handful of names (NVDA, AAPL, MSFT, GOOGL) score in the expected direction by eye. Two real bugs were caught building it: a negative year-over-year profit ratio raised to a fractional CAGR exponent silently produced a Python complex number that crashed the fundamentals cache, and Yahoo's free endpoint rate-limits hard after roughly 100-120 sequential per-ticker calls, which the first version handled by just dropping every later symbol from the output with no retry.
caveats: Not backtested -- the Decision Matrix bands (A+/A/B/Watchlist/Reject) are the checklist's own numbers, unvalidated against this universe's actual forward returns.

Institutional Interest (part of Supply/Demand) is a current holding level, not the FII/DII/MF trend the checklist actually wants -- no free API exposes the point-in-time shareholding history that would need.
Promoter Holding (part of Business Quality) uses Yahoo's insider-ownership field, which is not India's disclosed promoter-holding figure and is frequently blank or stale for NSE names.
Margin of Safety uses a Benjamin Graham formula (EPS x (8.5 + 2g)) as a single-number intrinsic-value stand-in, not a real DCF -- fine for ranking the universe, not for sizing a specific position.

The VCP leg reuses the EMA-VCP scanner's contraction/volume-dry-up detector but scores it against this checklist's own 0-10 bands, not the EMA-VCP backtest's own validated production thresholds -- cross-check a borderline VCP pass against EMA_VCP_BACKTEST_RESULTS.md before trusting it.

strategies.name: VCP Positional (volatility contraction pattern)
strategies.family: Daily base/contraction detector gated by a weekly trend/RS filter and a market-breadth filter
strategies.status_label: Backtested, provisional India-only edge -- watch only, not sized
strategies.headline: From a trader-supplied VCP checklist (Market check -> Weekly check -> Daily contraction pattern -> Volume check -> Pivot breakout -> Hourly entry timing -> 0-100 score -> entry/exit rules). A stock bases through 3+ shrinking pullback legs under a resistance pivot, with volume drying up through the base and expanding on the breakout bar, while its own weekly trend/relative-strength and the market's breadth are both healthy. Backtested on this project's own 1,003-name universe; the result is real but concentrated almost entirely in India.
entry: Base/contraction: the trailing 3+ swing-point legs ending at the most recent low each pull back less than the one before (10% tolerance, not strict), the final leg's depth is at most 8% (the checklist's literal 5% measured worse -- see Verdict), and the whole base spans at most ~130 daily bars (~6 months).
Pivot = the highest of the leg peaks bounding the base (the resistance the stock is coiling under, not the window's overall high).
Volume: the final leg's average volume is at most 70% of the earlier legs' average (dry-up), and leg volumes trend down leg-to-leg.

Weekly gate: price above a rising 30-week MA, within 15% of the 52-week high, the last two confirmed weekly swing highs AND lows both rising, and relative strength (trailing ~26-week return, ranked against the rest of the same market) in the top 30%.

Market gate: at least 50% of the stock's own market (US or India) trades above its own 200-day/40-week average -- this project's standard breadth proxy for 'index above its moving averages', since there is no real index series in the data.

Breakout: close crosses above the pivot with that bar's volume at least 1.4x its 50-day average (volume expansion -- the opposite condition from the dry-up checks above, both required). Entry is the next session's open.
exit: Stop: the final contraction leg's low (structural). If that is more than 10% away, the production build rejects the signal rather than taking an oversized risk.

Exit on whichever fires first: two daily closes below the 21 EMA (the checklist's own rule), a 4R target, or closing back below the pivot within 5 bars of entry ('failed breakout', the checklist's other named immediate-exit trigger). Of 169 trades: 92 exited via the 21-EMA trail, 34 via failed breakout, 25 at the stop, 18 at target -- the trailing exit does most of the work, but the failed-breakout rule earns its place too.
Costs of 0.20% round trip are charged in R, same as the rest of the reversal bot.
filters: The checklist's 0-100 score (Weekly Trend/20, Relative Strength/15, VCP Structure/15, Volume Dry-up/15, Final Tightness/10, Sector Strength/5, Breakout Volume/10, Market Trend/10) is computed and reported per signal, but is NOT a hard gate in the production build -- see Verdict for why.
This project has no real sector/industry data, so 'Sector Strength' and 'Relative Strength' in the score are the SAME trailing-return percentile reused twice, not independent information.
Runs daily in scan_US.bat / scan_India.bat, after the Weinstein Stage-2 scanner. Writes LATEST_VCP_<market>.json.
No concurrent-position cap or portfolio sizing yet -- same open gap as Weinstein and most of this project's other strategies.
strategies.verdict: Built 2026-11-01 from a trader-supplied checklist. The full production rule (daily pattern + weekly gate + volume checks + market gate) backtests to 169 trades, t=2.20, PF 1.67, avg R +0.251 over 26 years -- but that result is almost entirely an India effect: India alone is 55 trades, t=2.59, PF 2.83 (real); the 114 US trades are t=0.66 (statistical noise). An 8-variant ablation sweep found volume is where nearly all the measured edge lives -- removing the volume check collapses the daily result to pure noise (3,339 trades, t=0.24) despite the pattern geometry alone (no filters at all) still being weak at huge N (avg R 0.048). The weekly trend/RS gate's own contribution is genuinely ambiguous: removing it roughly quintuples the trade count and the t-stat goes UP, not down (3.80 vs 2.20) -- the opposite of what a weekly filter did for this project's EMA20-cross rule. The checklist's own score does not cleanly separate trade quality either: bucketed by score, the 70-80 bucket actually outperforms 80-85 and 85-90 (not monotonic); restricting to score >= 85 raises avg R and PF but the t-stat falls purely from the smaller sample. Running the identical engine on weekly bars directly gives only 12 trades in 26 years (58% win, PF 4.17) -- an attractive-looking but statistically meaningless sample. The checklist's hourly entry-timing step could barely be tested at all: the production signal is too rare to land inside yfinance's ~2.9-year hourly window even once across the usual pilot pool; an illustrative (not production) test on a looser variant found n=5, too small to mean anything, though directionally consistent with this project's other hourly work in finding that waiting for an hourly confirmation does not obviously help a daily swing entry.
caveats: This is provisional India-only evidence, not a validated system like v5/S1/S3: the US leg alone is not distinguishable from noise. Do not size this for US names off the numbers above.

No real sector or index data exists in this project -- 'sector outperforming the market' and 'strong relative strength' are the same single proxy (cross-sectional trailing-return rank within the same market), stated here rather than hidden.
The checklist's 'heavy distribution volume' immediate-exit trigger is not implemented -- too subjective to encode mechanically without faking a rule.

The 8% final-contraction cap (vs. the checklist's literal 5%) was picked by citing Minervini's own stated range, not by sweeping 6-10% to confirm it's a plateau rather than a lucky point -- the project's usual neighbourhood-sweep discipline was skipped here and should be done before trusting this number further.

stop_mode='pct_capped' (tighten the stop to 10% instead of rejecting wide-structural-risk setups) roughly doubles trade count on both daily and weekly with a similar or better t-stat -- looks like a real improvement, not yet adopted as the production default.
No concurrent-position cap or portfolio-level sizing was modelled, same simplification as weinstein_stage2.py.
rejected: The checklist's literal final-contraction cap (<=5%): fewer and weaker trades than the 8% default used here (131 trades, t=1.52 vs 169 trades, t=2.20) -- looser was better, not a cliff in the 'stricter wins' direction some trend-followers would expect.

Hard-gating entries on the score (score >= 85): trade count drops to 46 and the t-stat falls to 1.35 even though avg R and profit factor both rise -- a small-sample tradeoff, not demonstrated evidence the score threshold itself is predictive.

flows.title: SCAN_NOW.bat
flows.intro: Runs the whole reversal stack for both markets on demand. Safe at any time: the scans share one price cache and take an exclusive lock, so the second simply waits for the first.

steps.title: US reversal scan
steps.detail: Tops the price cache up to the latest close from Yahoo, then scans every symbol for v5, v6, S1, S3 and EMA20 cross + confirm setups on daily bars (weekly is scanned but unvalidated). Writes a dated Excel workbook and LATEST_US files.

steps.title: US revenue and dip scan
steps.detail: Finds stocks 15-40% off their high with RSI at or below 40 and a reversal day, checks the revenue trend, and saves the day's bars to Excel and CSV for future backtests.

steps.title: India reversal scan
steps.detail: The same scan on the Nifty 500 half of the universe.

steps.title: India revenue and dip scan
steps.detail: Same as the US one, with revenue from Yahoo.

steps.title: Market context classifier (both markets)
steps.detail: Tags every symbol as new-ATH breakout, inside a 300-day range, below/above its daily trendline, or a shallow/deep uptrend pullback, per MARKET_CONTEXT_FRAMEWORK.md. Writes LATEST_CONTEXT_<market>.json.

steps.title: Analog setup scanner (both markets)
steps.detail: Stage 1 + stages 2-4 combined: only looks for a live setup on stocks the context classifier currently tags NEW_ATH_BREAKOUT or DOWNTREND_BREAK, finds weekly base+breakout precedents per stock, backtests each one's retest on daily bars, and produces a live entry/stop/target plan gated on at least 2 confirmed precedents. Writes LATEST_ANALOG_<market>.json.

steps.title: Base + breakout scanner (both markets)
steps.detail: Stage 1 + stage 2 only, the wider screen: same context gate as the analog scanner, but lists every stock with a weekly base+breakout within the last 8 weeks, with no retest backtest and no 2-confirmed-analog requirement. Writes LATEST_BASEBREAKOUT_<market>.json.

steps.title: Paper-trade book
steps.detail: Records every new signal, replays each open trade from its entry bar so the book never double-counts, and scores live results against what the backtest predicted. Signals before the start date are NOT_TAKEN (no backfill) and signals refused by the 5-position cap are SKIPPED_CAP.

steps.title: Summary page
steps.detail: Builds one page combining the Reversal bot and the Revenue and dip scan for both markets and opens it in your browser.

flows.title: SETUP_SYSTEM_TASKS.bat
flows.intro: One-time setup, run as Administrator. Windows needs admin rights to create tasks that run as SYSTEM whether or not anyone is logged in.

steps.title: Create two daily tasks
steps.detail: ReversalScan_US every day at 07:00 runs scan_US.bat. ReversalScan_India every day at 19:00 runs scan_India.bat. First runs were set for 29 October 2026.

steps.title: Task settings
steps.detail: Start when available if the PC was asleep, wake the PC to run, ignore a second start if one is running, and stop after 60 minutes. Runs on battery.

steps.title: Desktop shortcut
steps.detail: Adds SCAN NOW - Revenue data to the desktop, which runs SCAN_NOW.bat.

steps.title: Proof run
steps.detail: Starts the US task once, waits up to 25 minutes, then prints the result code (0 means success) and the last lines of the US logs.

steps.title: Check the clock
steps.detail: The tasks use the PC's clock. If the PC is not on Singapore time, the script warns you that 07:00 and 19:00 are not Singapore times.

flows.title: SCAN NOW - Accumulation bot.bat
flows.intro: Scans US and India for institutional accumulation. Which markets run is set by MARKETS in settings.json.

steps.title: Find Python and packages
steps.detail: Locates Python and installs yfinance, pandas, numpy, requests, lxml, tzdata and xlsxwriter if any are missing.

steps.title: Download prices
steps.detail: The first run downloads about 2 years of prices for roughly 1,450 stocks and takes 5-10 minutes. Later runs only add new bars.

steps.title: Apply the checklist
steps.detail: Runs the preliminary tests, the seven points and the entry plan, then grades each stock A+ or A.

steps.title: Write reports
steps.detail: Saves latest_scan.html plus US and India pages and a CSV of the same rows, and archives the day's prices into eod_data as one Excel workbook per market per year.

steps.title: Scheduled version
steps.detail: run_scheduled_scan.bat US or IN is what the Windows tasks call. Telegram alerts can be turned on in settings.json.

website.title: GitHub Actions refreshes market data
website.detail: A free scheduled job on GitHub's servers fetches prices, company data, SEC Form 4 and filings, news and sentiment, and saves them as small JSON files. No paid service is involved.

website.title: Your PC publishes the Technical page

website.title: GitHub Pages serves the site
